CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual examination

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Andrea is a 52-year-old female with a past medical history of rheumatoid arthritis, atrial fibrillation, and reflux presenting for her annual exam. For her rheumatoid arthritis, she reports she has been walking, exercising, and doing yoga as recommended, which has significantly helped with her symptoms. She denies any joint pain, stiffness, or flare-ups over the past year and continues methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly without issues. Regarding her atrial fibrillation, she continues to experience palpitations, with the most recent episode approximately one week ago. She has noticed that stress triggers her palpitations and has attempted meditation and running with her dog to manage stress with limited relief. An event monitor was performed last month. For her reflux, she has implemented dietary modifications including cutting out soda and reports good symptom control with medication. She has not had any reflux flare-ups in over five months.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient endorses palpitations and nasal congestion related to allergies. She denies chest pain, shortness of breath, nausea, vomiting, or other concerning symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Rheumatoid arthritis
Atrial fibrillation
Reflux

MEDICATIONS
Methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly
Protonix 40 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Allergies (contributing to nasal congestion)

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient exercises regularly including walking, yoga, and running with her dog.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Heart rate well-controlled and regular
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm, 2/6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated (previously noted, not concerning)
Lungs: Clear bilaterally
Right elbow: Edema and erythema with pain to palpation
Extremities: No lower extremity edema

RESULTS
Event Monitor: Shows patient with intermittent atrial fibrillation with conversion pause, characterized by episodes of a-fib followed by pause then return to regular rhythm
Autoimmune Panel: Normal, indicating well-controlled rheumatoid arthritis on current therapy

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Rheumatoid arthritis: Stable. Continue methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly. Refill ordered. Rheumatology referral as needed.
2. Atrial fibrillation: Patient with intermittent a-fib and conversion pause. Refer to cardiology for cardiac ablation to map and eliminate arrhythmia focus to maintain normal sinus rhythm.
3. Reflux: Well-controlled on current regimen. Continue protonix 40 mg daily. Continue dietary modifications including avoidance of coffee and spicy foods.
